exposure: Thallium (I) sulfate administered via dosed drinking water
cohort: Time-mated Sprague Dawley rats (F0 dams and their F1 offspring) and adult male and female B6C3F1/N mice were used.
finding: Thallium (I) sulfate at concentrations of 12.5 mg/L in rats and 25 mg/L in mice resulted in decreased body weight gains and onset of whole-body alopecia, with significant maternal transfer of thallium to offspring.
followup_time: Up to postnatal day 28 for rat offspring and up to 2 weeks for adult mice.
gest_age: Exposure started from gestation day 6; fetuses were analyzed at gestation day 18.
